source.title: Do We Train on Test Data? The Impact of Near-Duplicates on License Plate Recognition
source.authors: R. Laroca; Valter Estevam; A. Britto; R. Minetto; David Menotti

record.tranche_reason: The study trains OCR models on original and duplicate-free natural-data splits and reports how recognition rates change, refining the generalization claim by showing that near-duplicates can inflate held-out results. It does not test random-label memorization or the listed claim versions directly.
record.gate_note: The study reports recognition rates for six OCR models under original and duplicate-free AOLP and CCPD protocols. Its duplicate counts and cited findings are not separate rows because they do not report model outcomes under an intervention.
record.test_reason: The study tests near-duplicate contamination of license-plate recognition benchmarks, which fits none of V1–V8. It does not measure random-label fitting, architecture width, convolution versus fully connected networks, optimizer or batch effects, dropout, sharpness, or influence-defined memorization removal versus random removal. The record's T5 classification is therefore unwarranted.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is substantively accurate: the authors conclude that near-duplicates bias LPR evaluation and development, with lower recognition rates under fair splits and changed rankings on AOLP. CCPD average recognition falls from 80.3% to 77.6%, with rankings largely preserved. Their significance language is qualitative; no statistical uncertainty or significance tests are reported.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares OCR training and evaluation under original versus duplicate-free dataset splits; it does not reproduce the original sources' methods. Models use Adam or Adadelta and synthetic data augmentation.
record.method_sensitivity: The recognition-rate decrease varies by dataset protocol and model; model rankings also change on AOLP, while CCPD rankings remain practically the same.

fits_no_version.finding: All six models have lower recognition rates under fair protocols: decreases of 1.80–3.64 percentage points on AOLP-A, 1.28–3.13 on AOLP-B, and 1.17–5.20 on CCPD. AOLP rankings change; CCPD rankings change only in fourth and fifth place.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training–test overlap in plate identity can inflate measured license-plate recognition performance and affect model rankings; the magnitude depends on the model and split protocol.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE International Joint Conference on Neural Network (IJCNN 2023)
record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported. The comparisons concern only two datasets and six OCR models; duplicate-free AOLP-B and CCPD protocols alter test or training/validation membership as described, so the split comparisons are not identical interventions across datasets.
record.rows_left_out: none; Table I, Table II and Table III model-level recognition rates are included. Table IV breaks CCPD performance down by subset but was omitted because it is an additional breakdown of the same six models and protocol comparison and the row cap is not binding; no claim version names subset-level behavior.

untested.parts: Paired random-label and natural-label training, training fit, and held-out performance relative to chance.
Width sweeps beyond zero training error and their test-error trajectory.
Controlled convolutional versus fully connected comparisons and effects of local connectivity or initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer comparisons under specified tuning budgets and recipe changes.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that recover performance.
Dropout interventions and interactions with training-set size, augmentation and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization gaps, and ranking against norm- or margin-based measures.
Influence-defined memorization scores and retraining after removing highly memorized versus equally many random training examples.

record.verdict_notes: All 18 numerical comparisons match the supplied tables and are the authors' own experiments. Their decreases are observed for the separate contamination finding; cannot_determine refers to their inability to establish any listed claim version. Random synthetic plate strings are rendered with correct labels, not fixed random-label assignments as in V1. Near-duplicate identity is not influence-defined memorization as in V8, whose original source is cited only for background.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural labels for the same architectures and recipes.
Network width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizer generalization comparisons and the stated tuning or recipe variations.
Large versus small batch comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout comparisons and its interactions with training-set size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness measurements and comparisons with other generalization measures.
Removing the most memorized training examples and comparing test accuracy with random-example removal.
